resolutions.researcher_notes: REUSED from batches/india-gas/staging/register-crosswalk/staged_resolutions.json (already staged, not redone). PNGRB NGPL-MIS Report, May 2026 edition, operational section, Sr. No. 16: 'Shahdol-Phulpur', entity RGPL, authorised 312.0 km / 3.5 MMSCMD, operating 304.0 km, authorisation date 11.07.2013 -- filed under 'OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE', consistent with the sheet's Status = 'operating'. Regulator-origin source, independent of the GAIL/GSPL/IOCL company reports GEM otherwise draws on. Value UNCHANGED; ref-only addition.

RGPL's own operator page (fetched and read directly) describes SHPPL as 'a natural gas pipeline' -- direct support for Fuel = Gas. Business Standard (independent press, 9 Jun 2017) names it the 'Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline' and describes it carrying CBM gas from Sohagpur to GAIL's HBJ network. Two independent origins (operator + press), both confirming natural gas as the fuel.

RGPL's own page describes SHPPL explicitly as 'designed as a common carrier system for gas transmission and distribution' -- literal word 'transmission'. Business Standard corroborates by describing RGPL as having 'laid' a pipeline that 'connects' the Sohagpur CBM fields to GAIL's HBJ trunk 'pipeline Network' -- i.e. a long-haul trunk connector to the national gas grid, consistent with a transmission line (not a gathering/process line -- the RIL gas-gathering stations at the field are a separate, upstream facility per the deep-sweep audit of this row). Two independent origins.

Business Standard, dated 9 Jun 2017, reports CBM production 'started on March 24 this year' and 'is currently being supplied for commissioning the Shahdol Phulpur Pipeline (SHPPL)' -- contemporaneous evidence the pipeline was being brought into service in 2017, supporting StartYear1 = 2017. Single strong contemporaneous source only (no second independent source with an explicit year found); PNGRB's 11.07.2013 date on this line is an AUTHORISATION date, not commissioning, and is deliberately NOT substituted per country guidance. Tier medium, single-source.

resolutions.researcher_notes: REUSED from the register-crosswalk (already staged, not redone). PNGRB's Authorised Length = 312.0 km matches LengthKnown exactly. CAVEAT (documented in the deep-sweep audit, not acted on here per standing rule against silently changing values): the register's own 'Operating Length' column reads 304 km for this line, and RGPL's site independently describes a '16" diameter x 304 km main pipeline', with Business Standard (2017) reporting RGPL 'laid a 302 km' pipeline -- i.e. the BUILT/operating length is consistently reported 8-10 km shorter than the AUTHORISED 312 km the sheet carries. Both figures are real and independently documented; this is an authorised-vs-built distinction, not a sourcing error, so the recorded value (312) is left UNCHANGED and cited to its own matching source (authorised length) rather than swapped for a different value. Flagging for Update/QC review rather than fabricating agreement.

RGPL's own page names the source precisely: 'Coal Bed Methane (CBM) blocks, located in the districts of Shahdol and Anuppur ... Sohagpur East (SP-E) and Sohagpur West (SP-W)'. Business Standard corroborates verbatim -- RGPL 'laid a 302 km Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline that connects Sohagpur CBM fields from Shahdol' -- literal match to the sheet's 'Sohagpur CBM Fields'. Two independent origins.

RGPL's own page states the route explicitly and completely: 'from Shahdol in Madhya Pradesh to Phulpur in Uttar Pradesh' where it 'hooks up with GAIL's existing Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) Pipeline Network' -- exact match for StartLocation=Shadol/Madhya Pradesh and EndLocation=Phulpur/Uttar Pradesh. Business Standard independently corroborates the Shahdol-to-Phulpur route ('a 302 km Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline that connects Sohagpur CBM fields from Shahdol to ... GAIL at Phulpur') though it does not itself name Uttar Pradesh explicitly. Two independent origins agree on both endpoints; the state-level detail rests primarily on RGPL.
